items.english: Hot. Sweat welled up prickling on his brow, and no sooner had it beaded than it ran lukewarm toward his eyes. As ill luck would have it, he was bound with thin cord, so of course he could not put out a hand to wipe it away. When he tried moving his neck to turn the sweat from its course, he felt at that instant a violent dizziness coming on, so to his regret he gave up that plan too. Meanwhile the sweat unceremoniously wet his eyelids and ran by the side of his nose and round his mouth to under his chin. Exceedingly nasty.

Until then he had lain with his eyes open, staring hard at the sky scorched white and the hemp field with its drooping leaves, but once the sweat began to run unchecked he had to give even that up. It was then that Liu learned for the first time that sweat stings when it gets in the eyes. So with the face of a sheep in the slaughterhouse, he meekly shut his eyes and lay baking in the sun, and presently he began to feel a certain pain in the skin of every upturned part of him, face or body alike. Over the whole surface of the skin, forces seemed to be at work pulling in every direction, while the skin itself had not a hair of spring to answer them. Everywhere prickled — that perhaps best describes the pain. This was not the misery of merely sweating. Liu began to find it a little hateful that he had taken the barbarian monk's cure.
notes: I was unsure of汗所 in the last lines, which I took as merely being sweaty rather than a clinical term, to keep the sensation flat as the reading asks.
